# Mobile-First Thinking

#### Course: Rapid Build With Claude Code

## Mobile-First Thinking

SpeedBlip is designed to work on any device. But "works on any device" is not a design decision - it is a consequence of making specific design decisions first.

Before building, I defined three breakpoints:

- 375px - Mobile (iPhone SE / most Android phones)
- 768px - Tablet (iPad portrait, smaller laptops)
- 1280px - Desktop (standard laptop and larger)

Mobile-first means you design the 375px layout first. Then you progressively enhance it for larger screens. This is the right order because it forces you to decide what is essential - there is no room for decoration on a 375px screen.

For SpeedBlip, designing mobile first revealed immediately that the sidebar navigation would not work on small screens. That decision led directly to the bottom navigation bar - a separate nav component that only renders below the tablet breakpoint. Planning this before coding meant I could include it in Chunk 2a's prompt clearly and completely.
